commands.name: init
commands.summary: Write sealmark.yaml (and sealmark.local.yaml for secrets) from an MCP client's configuration, a one-line command, or a template. With --probes, start the server like doctor does and write one valid call per tool as a probes: block (never asks a question).

commands.name: run
commands.summary: Grade the configured server(s) and print the report.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Check that sealmark can start your server: tools on PATH, the launcher, the sandbox, initialize and tools/list, the classification and why each pack would run or not.

commands.name: describe
commands.summary: Print the machine-readable description of this build: methodology and CLI versions, the check registry, configuration keys, commands, flags and exit codes.

commands.name: explain
commands.summary: Explain one check: what it measures, its probes, verdict rules, known false positives and negatives, the settings that affect it, and what to fix when it fails.

commands.name: list-checks
commands.summary: List every check with its pack, severity, scope and whether its settings are locked by the standard profile.

commands.name: diff
commands.summary: Compare two JSON reports without running anything: verdict regressions and improvements, and tool-surface drift. Exit 1 when something regressed or drifted.

args.name: before.json
args.description: The earlier JSON report (a --write-baseline file or --format json output).

commands.name: config show
commands.summary: Print the merged configuration, with the origin of every value on request.

commands.name: config profiles
commands.summary: List shipped and user profiles with their difference from the standard profile.

commands.name: config migrate
commands.summary: Rewrite a configuration file from an older schema_version to the current one and print the diff.

flags.name: --config
flags.description: Project config file (default sealmark.yaml).
flags.doc: Project config file (default sealmark.yaml).

flags.name: --profile
flags.description: Profile to start from.
flags.doc: Profile to start from.

flags.name: --url
flags.description: URL of the MCP server to test (Streamable HTTP). With --start, Sealmark starts the server and waits for this URL to answer.
flags.doc: URL of the MCP server to test (Streamable HTTP). With --start, Sealmark starts the server and waits for this URL to answer.

flags.name: --start
flags.description: Command line that starts the server, for example --start "my-server --port 8000". With --url it is launched, awaited, tested and stopped; alone it is a stdio server. It is not run through a shell: no &&, |, ;, > or & and no VAR=value prefix (wrap it: --start "sh -c '...'").
flags.doc: Command line that starts the server, for example --start "my-server --port 8000". With --url it is launched, awaited, tested and stopped; alone it is a stdio server. It is not run through a shell: no &&, |, ;, > or & and no VAR=value prefix (wrap it: --start "sh -c '...'").

flags.name: --header
flags.description: HTTP header for --url as "Name: value"; repeat for several. Put a CI secret in single quotes, --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_TOKEN}', and Sealmark reads it from the environment, so it never shows in the process list.
flags.doc: HTTP header for --url as "Name: value"; repeat for several. Put a CI secret in single quotes, --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_TOKEN}', and Sealmark reads it from the environment, so it never shows in the process list.

flags.name: --bearer
flags.description: Bearer token for --url: sets the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. Put a CI secret in single quotes, --bearer '${MCP_TOKEN}', and Sealmark reads it from the environment. Easier than --header in a CI file, because "Authorization: Bearer x" contains ": " and breaks a plain YAML value.
flags.doc: Bearer token for --url: sets the header Authorization: Bearer <token>. Put a CI secret in single quotes, --bearer '${MCP_TOKEN}', and Sealmark reads it from the environment. Easier than --header in a CI file, because "Authorization: Bearer x" contains ": " and breaks a plain YAML value.

flags.name: --start-timeout
flags.description: Seconds to wait for --start's server to answer on --url (default 60).
flags.doc: Seconds to wait for --start's server to answer on --url (default 60).

flags.name: --name
flags.description: Display name of the server in the report.
flags.doc: Display name of the server in the report.

flags.name: --soft-fail
flags.description: A grade below the gate prints a warning and exits 0. Config errors, nothing graded and server failures still fail.
flags.doc: A grade below the gate prints a warning and exits 0. Config errors, nothing graded and server failures still fail.

flags.name: --pack
flags.description: Test suite (pack) to run; repeat for several. --suite is the same flag.
flags.doc: Test suite (pack) to run; repeat for several. --suite is the same flag.

flags.name: --suite
flags.description: Test suite to run; repeat for several. Same as --pack.
flags.doc: Test suite to run; repeat for several. Same as --pack.

flags.name: --timeout-probe
flags.description: Seconds the cap and timeout probes wait.
flags.doc: Seconds the cap and timeout probes wait.

flags.name: --connect-timeout
flags.description: Seconds to wait for the server to start.
flags.doc: Seconds to wait for the server to start.

flags.name: --fail-under
flags.description: Exit 1 when a graded pack is below this letter. Default A: anything below an A fails. Use B, C, D or F to relax it, or none to turn the gate off.
flags.doc: Exit 1 when a graded pack is below this letter. Default A: anything below an A fails. Use B, C, D or F to relax it, or none to turn the gate off.

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Report format; repeat the flag or comma-separate for several (text, json, markdown, junit, sarif, summary, badge, shields).
flags.doc: Report format; repeat the flag or comma-separate for several (text, json, markdown, junit, sarif, summary, badge, shields).

flags.name: --out
flags.description: Write the report to this file.
flags.doc: Write the report to this file.

flags.name: --out-dir
flags.description: Directory for multi-format output.
flags.doc: Directory for multi-format output.

flags.name: --template
flags.description: Report template path.
flags.doc: Report template path.

flags.name: --baseline
flags.description: Prior JSON report to compare against.
flags.doc: Prior JSON report to compare against.

flags.name: --write-baseline
flags.description: Write the current JSON report for later --baseline runs.
flags.doc: Write the current JSON report for later --baseline runs.

flags.name: --fail-on
flags.description: With a baseline, what decides the exit code: any (the default), regressions or drift; repeat the flag or comma-separate for several.
flags.doc: With a baseline, what decides the exit code: any (the default), regressions or drift; repeat the flag or comma-separate for several.

flags.name: --verbosity
flags.description: quiet, normal or verbose.
flags.doc: quiet, normal or verbose.

flags.name: --redact
flags.description: --no-redact prints secret-looking values (local debugging only).
flags.doc: --no-redact prints secret-looking values (local debugging only).

flags.name: --embedded
flags.description: --no-embedded disables the embedded Postgres.
flags.doc: --no-embedded disables the embedded Postgres.

flags.name: --pg
flags.description: Superuser DSN of an existing Postgres (needs --yes).
flags.doc: Superuser DSN of an existing Postgres (needs --yes).

flags.name: --yes
flags.description: run: confirm that --pg may recreate the seed database. init: take the defaults and never ask questions.
flags.doc: run: confirm that --pg may recreate the seed database. init: take the defaults and never ask questions.

flags.name: --active
flags.description: Allow the exec pack and active custom probes.
flags.doc: Allow the exec pack and active custom probes.

flags.name: --sandbox
flags.description: --no-sandbox disables the sandbox (the run becomes CUSTOM).
flags.doc: --no-sandbox disables the sandbox (the run becomes CUSTOM).

flags.name: --sandbox-dir
flags.description: Parent directory for the sandbox.
flags.doc: Parent directory for the sandbox.

flags.name: --keep-sandbox
flags.description: Keep the sandbox after the run.
flags.doc: Keep the sandbox after the run.

flags.name: --pack-timeout
flags.description: Seconds before one pack is abandoned.
flags.doc: Seconds before one pack is abandoned.

flags.name: --upstream
flags.description: Start the harness's upstream stub (upstream.kind: http) and fill {upstream} in the server config with its URL, so the scope, sql-guard and upstream packs can see what the server forwards.
flags.doc: Start the harness's upstream stub (upstream.kind: http) and fill {upstream} in the server config with its URL, so the scope, sql-guard and upstream packs can see what the server forwards.

flags.name: --scope-tool
flags.description: A tool that takes an identifier the server restricts, as tool=param (for example describe_table=table); repeat for several. Needs --scope-allow.
flags.doc: A tool that takes an identifier the server restricts, as tool=param (for example describe_table=table); repeat for several. Needs --scope-allow.

flags.name: --scope-allow
flags.description: An identifier the server may serve; an entry ending with the separator is a prefix (sales.public.). Repeat for several.
flags.doc: An identifier the server may serve; an entry ending with the separator is a prefix (sales.public.). Repeat for several.

flags.name: --scope-deny
flags.description: An identifier the server must refuse even inside the allow list. Repeat for several.
flags.doc: An identifier the server must refuse even inside the allow list. Repeat for several.

flags.name: --identity-a
flags.description: Token for caller A ({bearer}, {bearer:a}) when the server validates tokens it did not issue. Put a CI secret in single quotes, --identity-a '${TOKEN_A}', and Sealmark reads it from the environment.
flags.doc: Token for caller A ({bearer}, {bearer:a}) when the server validates tokens it did not issue. Put a CI secret in single quotes, --identity-a '${TOKEN_A}', and Sealmark reads it from the environment.

flags.name: --identity-b
flags.description: Token for caller B ({bearer:b}); must differ from --identity-a. Single-quote a CI secret as for --identity-a.
flags.doc: Token for caller B ({bearer:b}); must differ from --identity-a. Single-quote a CI secret as for --identity-a.

flags.name: --oauth
flags.description: Start the harness's stub OAuth issuer (oauth.issuer: stub): {issuer}, {jwks} and {audience} name it for the server's own settings, and the harness sends tokens it signed as Authorization: Bearer. The oauth pack then checks that forged, expired, wrong-audience and wrong-issuer tokens are refused.
flags.doc: Start the harness's stub OAuth issuer (oauth.issuer: stub): {issuer}, {jwks} and {audience} name it for the server's own settings, and the harness sends tokens it signed as Authorization: Bearer. The oauth pack then checks that forged, expired, wrong-audience and wrong-issuer tokens are refused.

flags.name: --oauth-tls
flags.description: --no-oauth-tls serves the stub issuer over plain http instead of https (the default, with a throwaway CA in {ca_file}). Only for a server that cannot be given a CA file; a hardened server refuses an http trust root.
flags.doc: --no-oauth-tls serves the stub issuer over plain http instead of https (the default, with a throwaway CA in {ca_file}). Only for a server that cannot be given a CA file; a hardened server refuses an http trust root.

flags.name: --server
flags.description: Entry of `servers` to use (run also accepts `all`). init: the imported servers to write, as comma separated names, client/name, or all.
flags.doc: Entry of `servers` to use (run also accepts `all`). init: the imported servers to write, as comma separated names, client/name, or all.

flags.name: --help
flags.description: Print usage and exit.
flags.doc: Print usage and exit.

flags.name: --version
flags.description: Print the sealmark version and exit.
flags.doc: Print the sealmark version and exit.

flags.name: --force
flags.description: Overwrite files that already exist.
flags.doc: Overwrite files that already exist.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: Machine-readable output.
flags.doc: Machine-readable output.

flags.name: --probes
flags.description: init: start the server like doctor does and write one valid call per tool as a probes: block (stdout, or the config file with --write). Never prompts.
flags.doc: init: start the server like doctor does and write one valid call per tool as a probes: block (stdout, or the config file with --write). Never prompts.

flags.name: --write
flags.description: init --probes: append the block to the config file; exit 2 when it already has a probes: key.
flags.doc: init --probes: append the block to the config file; exit 2 when it already has a probes: key.

flags.name: --from
flags.description: Write a config from a one-liner, for example --from "npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem {sandbox}".
flags.doc: Write a config from a one-liner, for example --from "npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem {sandbox}".

flags.name: --ci
flags.description: Print a ready-to-paste CI job for this provider and write nothing.
flags.doc: Print a ready-to-paste CI job for this provider and write nothing.

flags.name: --from-url
flags.description: Write a config for an already running Streamable HTTP server.
flags.doc: Write a config for an already running Streamable HTTP server.

flags.name: --client
flags.description: Only read this MCP client's configuration (claude-desktop, claude-code, cursor, vscode, copilot-cli).
flags.doc: Only read this MCP client's configuration (claude-desktop, claude-code, cursor, vscode, copilot-cli).

flags.name: --effective
flags.description: Accepted for compatibility; config show always prints the effective configuration.
flags.doc: Accepted for compatibility; config show always prints the effective configuration.

flags.name: --origins
flags.description: Annotate every value with where it came from.
flags.doc: Annotate every value with where it came from.

flags.name: --replay
flags.description: Re-run with the locked settings of a previous JSON report, after verifying its config hash.
flags.doc: Re-run with the locked settings of a previous JSON report, after verifying its config hash.

flags.name: --fixture
flags.description: Write a fixture the sandbox generates, for hand runs: the fs layout, the git repositories or the SQLite database (DuckDB is planned).
flags.doc: Write a fixture the sandbox generates, for hand runs: the fs layout, the git repositories or the SQLite database (DuckDB is planned).

flags.name: --into
flags.description: Directory for --fixture.
flags.doc: Directory for --fixture.

exitCodes.meaning: a graded pack is below --fail-under (a provisional A* is below an A gate), an inconclusive pack under output.exit_policy.treat_inconclusive_as: fail, or a baseline comparison found a regression
harness or server failure (the server would not start, the database was unavailable, or doctor found a failing step)
